text.p: The following are the leading stories in the Maltese press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Euro-Med conference to be held in Malta next April. Foreign Minister George Vella told Maltese parliament that 27 foreign ministers from Europe and Mediterranean countries would meet in Malta on April 15 and 16 to review progress since first Euro-Med conference in Barcelona in November 1995.
- Police stop television station making illegal broadcasts. Smash TV is licensed to transmit via cable network, but on Wednesday made terrestial transmissions and was stopped by police.
- Man jailed for 20 years over wife's murder.

- Opposition suspends parliamentary pairing agreement with government in protest over Malta Drydocks Bill. The government wants the bill to be debated through all stages on Saturday, but the opposition says there is no urgency, and holding the debate on Saturday violates agreement that debates would be held a week after publication of draft laws. The bill changes the composition of the state-owned dockyard's managing council to give it majority government representation. Its members have been directly elected by the yard's workforce since 1975.
- Opposition spokesman claims government preparing to increase power tariffs.
